solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stress weighs down first pair to encounter incline

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the next, pressing down on it

parts.note: stress or worry is care

indicators.note: asks for the opening two letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A stressful image of weight pressing down at the first sight of a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To careen is to heel over or tilt, so it is a verb synonym of incline.

clue.text: Score with service at both ends, holding game

indicators.note: the end letters hold the game between them
only the two end letters of the word service are kept

parts.note: crib is short for cribbage, the card game

explanation.surface: A tennis scoreline: serving well at either end of a match while holding a service game.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribe is to mark a line by scratching, and to score is to cut a line in a surface.

clue.text: FBI come on the dot mobilising precise search-tool

indicators.note: setting the letters in motion so they move into new positions

explanation.surface: The FBI turn up punctually and deploy an exacting method of hunting for evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb with closely set teeth catches everything, hence a byword for a thorough, meticulous search.

clue.text: One's put on street — that's touching

parts.note: what one has put on, such as weight, is a gain: A plus GAIN

explanation.surface: Someone sets a thing down on the road, and it ends up in contact with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is A and 'put on' (as weight is put on) is GAIN, with the 's standing for has.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaning against a wall is touching it, so the preposition matches that sense.

clue.text: Friend of the Earth in endless jam — ain't it so awful!

indicators.note: the jam word loses its final letter

parts.note: conserve is fruit preserved with sugar, a jam

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are made a dreadful mess of, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: An environmental campaigner in a tight spot protests that things are dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts CONSERVE to CONSERV; 'awful' rearranges AINTITSO into ATIONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends of the Earth is an environmental group, so a friend of the Earth is someone protecting nature.

clue.text: Hand in notice editor allowed

indicators.note: the hand word goes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone handed in their notice and the editor permitted it.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitted can mean let in or permitted, a synonym of allowed in the past tense.

clue.text: Waggish setter's singular records

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous or knowing
the setter has, from the compiler's point of view, is I've
s is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A jokey compiler boasts of their unique track record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter's' is read as 'the setter has', giving I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents, i.e. records kept for reference.

clue.text: Charming and rich G-man among those getting the sack

parts.note: these two phrases are among the results of rearranging, by command, the letters of the word for walking in step

explanation.surface: A smooth, wealthy FBI agent finds himself among the people being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read as instructions, the answer says 'put the letters of MARCHING in new orders', and CHARMING and RICH G-MAN are two such orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given one's marching orders is an idiom for being dismissed, the same as getting the sack.

clue.text: See 8
26 in Caledonia, indigenously

indicators.note: the letters are found tucked inside the following words

explanation.surface: Referring to a native Scottish word for the answer at 26.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is OWN; in Scots dialect 'own' is ain, as in 'my ain folk'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for possessing something oneself is this dialect form, matching the solution to 26.

clue.text: Sounds like blackcurrant and sloe together perhaps can produce sickness

indicators.note: says the spoken form of the following phrase gives the entry

parts.note: a blackcurrant is a berry and so, loosely, is a sloe: two berries side by side

explanation.surface: Mixing two hedgerow fruits might make you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by lack of vitamin B1, so it is an example of a sickness.

clue.text: Son's flying shots regularly showing neglect

parts.note: s is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: take every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A son's wayward shooting reveals carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or disregard them, a verb synonym of neglect.

clue.text: Cool liquid in tremendous vat

indicators.note: fluid, not fixed, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Something chilled sits as fluid in an enormous tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool person is reserved and unemotional, which is what showing no feelings means.

clue.text: Slip into river

definitions.meaning: to put on clothing, as one slips into a coat
a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: Falling or sliding into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to put on a garment; the other names rivers in Russia, Scotland and Yorkshire.

clue.text: May one begin right away in cards?

parts.note: may in the sense of being permitted is can
a means one

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is taken out

parts.note: start means begin

explanation.surface: A card-player wonders whether to start immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is RT, not just R; 'away' takes RT out of START, leaving STA.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game, so a game played with cards.

clue.text: 'Self-sacrifice' commonplace under Capone, say …

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: Al Capone, the gangster, is an example of someone called Al
a truism is a commonplace, a statement too obvious to need saying

explanation.surface: A gangster's view that giving oneself up is just a platitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for others, putting their interests above one's own.

clue.text: … like Pharaoh, see, with finesse

parts.note: as means like
Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the Egyptian pharaoh
Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Continuing the gangster theme: something done as smoothly as a pharaoh would see it done.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something astutely means doing it shrewdly and cleverly, i.e. with skill and finesse.

clue.text: Drama with 50 checking out of the Parisian Grand — one finds somewhere to settle

indicators.note: the fifty leaves, as a guest leaving a hotel

parts.note: a play is a drama
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
des is French for 'of the' before a plural noun, in the Parisian tongue
K stands for a thousand, a grand

explanation.surface: A hotel scene: a guest checks out of a grand Parisian hotel and settles the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay-desk is a counter where bills are paid, so it is a place to settle up.

clue.text: Come a cropper in Kielder Reservoir

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble into a large Northumberland lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Kielder Water is a big reservoir in Northumberland, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is to fail or make a blunder, so a figurative synonym for making a mistake.

clue.text: Pants like yaks, maybe?

parts.note: underpants of a style named after a letter; words like yaks or yams begin with that letter

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some underwear resembles long-haired oxen.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer at its hyphen: 'yaks' has a Y at the front, as all such words do.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's briefs with a Y-shaped seam at the front, a kind of pants (British for underpants).

clue.text: Monument Station refit — tube's affected with loads of yuckiness initially

indicators.note: made to change, so the letters are rearranged
take the opening letters of the words

explanation.surface: A station being refitted has a tube line affected by a lot of muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges REFIT, TUBE and LOY (from 'initially') into TUEOFLIBERTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Statue of Liberty in New York harbour is a famous monument, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Trophies forming memories — or not at all?

indicators.note: the letters are moulded into a new shape
the word or is to be left out entirely

explanation.surface: Awards that create lasting recollections, or perhaps none whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming' rearranges MEMORIES once 'not at all' removes OR from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmies are the annual US television awards, statuettes given as trophies.

clue.text: Position climbing frames (one French) and prepare to play

indicators.note: the reversed word surrounds the French word
in a down entry the word goes upwards, written backwards

parts.note: to put something is to position it
une is French for one (feminine)

explanation.surface: Setting up a climbing frame and getting ready for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune up is to adjust an instrument before a performance, i.e. to get ready to play.

clue.text: Awkward moment briefly follows abortive trick

indicators.note: the moment word comes after the trick word
cut short before completion, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

indicators.note: shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tick is a moment

explanation.surface: An awkward pause follows a failed trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic can mean unsophisticated or clumsy, a sense of awkward.

clue.text: Honour's the last word in heart of true-born Tudors

indicators.note: the prayer word is placed inside the central letters
the central letters of the phrase are taken

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Royal pride in the genuine Tudor line.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle four letters, ORNT, of 'true-born Tudors' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described as an ornament to their profession brings it honour, so ornament means a source of credit.

clue.text: Confess, darling!

definitions.meaning: as in 'my ...', a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A lover urges their sweetheart to come clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fault is to admit it; 'my own' addresses a loved one.

clue.text: Retreat from compound holding stragglers from fearless army

indicators.note: the compound wraps around the picked letters

parts.note: alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate

indicators.note: stragglers trail at the back, so the final letters

explanation.surface: Withdrawing from a fortified camp with the stragglers of a bold army.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum is a place of refuge or sanctuary, a retreat.

clue.text: Pleasing composition of Rossini avoids undisciplined flirtatiousness

indicators.note: the letters of the composer's name are to be kept clear of the result
unruly, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Rossini piece is agreeable because it steers clear of wild coquetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' removes ROSSINI from FLIRTATIOUSNESS and 'undisciplined' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means showing good aesthetic judgement, hence attractive and pleasing.
